what_its_for: Tafluprost eye drops are used to lower pressure inside your eye. High eye pressure can damage your optic nerve and lead to a condition called glaucoma, which can cause vision loss. This medicine helps protect your eyesight by keeping the pressure in your eye at a safe level.
how_to_take: Use tafluprost only in your eye — never swallow it. Wash your hands thoroughly before and after use. Tilt your head back, pull down your lower eyelid to form a small pocket, and place one drop into that pocket. Close your eye gently for 1 to 2 minutes and press lightly on the inner corner of your eye near your nose. This helps keep the medicine in your eye. If you wear contact lenses, remove them before using the drops and wait at least 15 minutes before putting them back in. If you use other eye drops, wait at least 5 minutes between each medication.
dosing: Use one drop in the affected eye or eyes once every evening. It is best to use it at the same time each evening to get the most benefit. Do not use more drops than prescribed — using more will not lower your eye pressure better and may cause side effects.
missed_dose: If you forget to use your drop in the evening, skip the missed dose and use your next dose the following evening at your regular time. Do not use two doses in one day to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store unopened pouches in the refrigerator between 36°F and 46°F (2°C and 8°C). Once you open a pouch, you can store the individual unit-dose containers at room temperature up to 77°F (25°C) for up to 28 days. Keep each unit-dose container in the foil pouch to protect it from light. Throw away any unit-dose containers that have been open for more than 28 days. Keep this medicine out of reach of children.
what_to_avoid: Avoid touching the tip of the dropper to your eye, fingers, or any surface to prevent contamination and infection. Do not use tafluprost while wearing contact lenses — always remove them first and wait 15 minutes before reinserting. Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery right after using the drops until your vision clears. Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, as this medicine may not be safe during pregnancy.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away if you experience: sudden vision changes or vision loss, severe eye pain or redness, signs of an eye infection such as discharge or swelling, swelling or changes around your eye or eyelid, an eye injury, or if you are scheduled for eye surgery. Also call your doctor if you notice your eye color changing (the iris may gradually become more brown), your eyelashes growing longer or darker, or increased darkness of the skin around your eye, as these are known side effects of this type of medicine.
when_it_works: Tafluprost starts working within a few hours of your first dose, but it may take a few weeks of regular use before your eye pressure is fully controlled. Your doctor will check your eye pressure at follow-up visits to make sure the medicine is working properly. Keep using it every day even if your eyes feel fine, because high eye pressure usually has no noticeable symptoms.
special_populations: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant or breastfeeding — tafluprost is generally not recommended during pregnancy. This medicine has not been well studied in children, so talk to your doctor before using it in anyone under 18. If you have had eye surgery, inflammation inside your eye (uveitis), or wear contact lenses regularly, let your doctor know before starting this medicine. Older adults can generally use tafluprost safely, but should still report any new symptoms to their doctor.
